reason: Builds a model|host price index used to price usage events that already happened. A host delisted today still priced yesterday's traffic, so excluding is_active=false here would silently leave real usage unpriced. Reviewed Dispatch 88.
Same price index, same reason: the demo prices historical slices against the price that applied, not against today's listing. Reviewed Dispatch 88.

The sync itself must see every model key it has ever written, including delisted ones, to decide what is genuinely new. Filtering to active would re-report old models as new on every run. Reviewed Dispatch 88.

Two reads, both of which must see delisted rows by design. The new-provider watch asks whether a host name has ever been priced, so that a relisted provider does not re-raise a parser task that was already solved; the delisting sweep exists precisely to read inactive rows and count their missed syncs. Neither read's output is ever quoted as a price: the first produces host names for the jobs board, the second updates lifecycle columns. The engine's own price reads (evaluate.server.ts, pipeline.functions.ts, dashboard.server.ts) all filter is_active, and delisted-price.integration.test.ts proves a delisted row cannot reach a recommendation. Reviewed Dispatch 110.
Reads referral attribution for one workspace by primary key through the caller's RLS-scoped client. There is no cross-tenant surface to contaminate. Reviewed Dispatch 88.

Reads one workspace's plan by primary key through the caller's RLS-scoped client, to decide that caller's own entitlement. is_synthetic is a cross-tenant mixing concern and there is no cross-tenant surface here: the row returned is the caller's own workspace, and a synthetic workspace is entitled to exactly the plan it holds. Surfaced by the Dispatch 127 scanner fix, which stopped this chain borrowing a neighbouring query's filters. Reviewed Dispatch 127.

Lists the workspaces the signed-in caller belongs to, through requireSupabaseAuth and the is_org_member RLS policy. Filtering is_synthetic here would hide the demo workspace from the one account permitted to see it while adding no isolation: RLS, not this filter, is what keeps other tenants out. Surfaced by the Dispatch 127 scanner fix. Reviewed Dispatch 127.

Reads one workspace's Stripe customer/subscription id by primary key, after the caller's membership has already been checked. is_synthetic guards against synthetic rows mixing into a real tenant's figures; there is no cross-tenant surface here and a synthetic workspace still has its own billing row. Reviewed Dispatch 231.

The sweep must list every workspace, synthetic included: the demo workspace's rollups are what the demo dashboard reads, so excluding them would leave exactly the coverage holes this job exists to repair. Nothing here is quoted as a customer figure; the output is per-workspace coverage state. Reviewed Dispatch 231.

Reads the one workspace named by a signature-verified Stripe event, by primary key, to apply that event's plan and referral attribution. Filtering is_synthetic would silently drop a real payment event if the workspace were ever flagged. Reviewed Dispatch 231.
